newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss private Bank Sarasin in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Swiss private Bank Sarasin in Geneva.

text.p: Swiss private Bank Sarasin & Co said on Friday it was opening a fully-owned Geneva operation with an eye mainly to Anglo-Saxon but also Latin American, Middle Eastern and Far Eastern clients.
Sarasin Geneva SA is the latest newcomer to this secretive Swiss hub for the very rich, where competition is heating up amid at least five private bank takeovers so far this year.
Bank Sarasin president Georg Krayer, also the chairman of the Swiss Bankers Association, said the bank's private assets grew 10 percent in 1997's first five months over a year ago.

New clients contributed to more than half of that growth and market performance the remainder, he told a news conference. "This year has been better than last year. Growth started in full force in January," Krayer said.
Switzerland has a 40 percent share of the world's offshore wealth and some $1.8 trillion in private assets under management, according to recent Swiss banking surveys.

Bank Sarasin & Co, based in Basle, with offices in Zurich and London and founded in 1841, has 5.5 billion Swiss francs under management for institutional clients and 2.0 billion Swiss francs under its mutual funds family.

But it does not publish assets under management for private clients as part of banking secrecy. With eight partners, it is considered to be one of Switzerland's top four strictly private banks where the partners have unlimited liability.
Despite growing competition, Swiss bankers say private banking business remains a cash cow, contributing to more than half of profits at the big Swiss banks.
This month, Belgian Cera Bank announced it bought the Geneva-based Swiss Inca Bank SA, a month after Swiss Gotthard Bank acquired a 75 percent stake in Banque de Gestion Privee.
